title: Tallest Branch in a Binary Tree
statement:
You are given the root node of a binary tree, where each node holds an integer value and has references to at most two children, `left` and `right` (either may be absent).

Define the *depth* of the tree as the number of nodes encountered along the longest path that starts at the root and travels down to any leaf (a leaf is a node with no children). In other words, it is the count of nodes on the deepest root-to-leaf path.

Write a function that computes this maximum depth. If the tree is empty (the root is absent), the depth is 0.

examples.input: root = [4, 2, 7, 1, 3, 6, 9]  (a complete binary tree of height 3: node 4 has children 2 and 7; node 2 has children 1 and 3; node 7 has children 6 and 9)
examples.explanation: The longest root-to-leaf path visits 3 nodes, e.g., 4 -> 2 -> 1 (or any path down to one of the four leaves), so the depth is 3.

examples.input: root = [5, null, 8, null, 12]  (node 5 has only a right child 8, and node 8 has only a right child 12, forming a rightward chain)
examples.explanation: The tree is a single chain 5 -> 8 -> 12 with no branching, so the deepest path contains all 3 nodes.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is between 0 and 10^4.
The tree structure is a valid binary tree (each node has at most one parent).
